en.title: Village life
en.summary: What daily life in a village looks like and how it is changing.

paragraphs: Village life is quieter and more community-centred than city life. This lesson describes a typical English village and teaches you to use there is and there are in descriptions.

A typical English village has a church, a pub, a village hall, a small shop with a post office and a green. In the past most inhabitants worked on farms, but today many commute to a nearby town. Shops, schools and buses have disappeared from many villages, although community groups sometimes run them. A newcomer chats with a neighbour.

lines.speaker: Newcomer
lines.text: Is there a shop in the village?

lines.speaker: Neighbour
lines.text: Yes, there's a small shop with a post office. And there's a pub, a church and a village hall.

lines.speaker: Neighbour
lines.text: Only twice a day. Most people have a car, because you can't manage without one.

lines.speaker: Newcomer
lines.text: What happens in the village hall?

lines.speaker: Neighbour
lines.text: There are all kinds of events: a monthly market, yoga classes, and the parish council meets there.

lines.speaker: Newcomer
lines.text: It sounds like a close community.

lines.speaker: Neighbour
lines.text: It is. Everyone is welcome, as long as they join in.

paragraphs: **1. There is and there are with lists.** When a list follows, the verb often agrees with the first noun. See Introduction to Grammar: Present tense, being and having.

blocks.html:
FormExample
there isThere is a pub and a church.
there areThere are two shops.
there used to beThere used to be a school.
there will beThere will be a fair in June.

paragraphs: **2. Only plus frequency, and as long as.** Only limits a number; as long as sets a condition. See Introduction to Grammar: Adverbs.

blocks.html:
FormExample
only twice a dayThe bus runs only twice a day.
as long asEveryone is welcome as long as they join in.
provided thatYou can join provided that you pay.
can't manage withoutYou can't manage without a car.

items: The village green is a grassy space in the centre.
The parish council deals with local matters.
The village hall hosts meetings, classes and parties.
A community is a group of people living in a place.

paragraphs: Many villages have lost shops and buses, but community groups often run them with the help of volunteers. A few villages have bought their own pub, so that it is not turned into a house.
